title: Programming-Tactus: Write/align Agent primitive chapters (tools/toolsets + call pattern)
description:
Update Programming-Tactus Agent-related chapters that are currently stubs and/or contain stale API references. Target at least: chapters/04-agent-configuration.qmd, chapters/05-agent-interactions.qmd, chapters/08-tool-integration.qmd.

Key alignments:
- Use canonical Agent call style (call the agent value like a function) and document per-turn overrides via tools = {...}.
- Use Toolset primitive + composition into Agent.tools (avoid legacy toolsets key).
- Include a deterministic testing section (tactus test --mock + Mocks { ... }).
creator: Ryan Alyn Porter

custom.beads_acceptance_criteria: - No mention of Agent("name").turn() unless it is actually supported and documented in canonical Tactus docs\n- Replace vague 'toolsets' wording with precise Toolset primitive + tools = {...} examples\n- Add at least one runnable code snippet per chapter (or explicitly link to a runnable example in Tactus-examples)
custom.beads_close_reason: Filled Programming-Tactus agent chapters 04/05/08 with canonical Agent/tools/toolset patterns; removed stale Agent(name).turn reference; Quarto render succeeds; Programming-Tactus CI green.
custom.beads_notes:
Outline / writing notes for Programming-Tactus agent chapters

Source-of-truth (this repo): docs/agent-primitive.md, SPECIFICATION.md, and implementation in tactus/primitives/handles.py (AgentHandle is callable).

Chapter 04-agent-configuration.qmd (config reference)
- What goes in Agent { ... }:
  - provider, model, system_prompt
  - tools = {...} (Tool + Toolset handles, and optionally toolset aliases by string if supported)
  - optional model/provider params if supported (temperature/max_tokens/etc) - confirm against code before documenting.
- Toolsets vs tools:
  - Define Toolset { tools = {...} } and pass it inside Agent.tools
  - Prefer 'tools = {...}' everywhere; avoid legacy 'toolsets = {...}'.
- Per-turn capability control:
  - agent({message = ..., tools = {}}) for no-tools summarization
  - agent({tools = {search, done}}) for explicit capability boundary
- Testing story teaser: keep control flow in Procedure; mock agent/tool calls in specs.

Chapter 05-agent-interactions.qmd (calling + per-turn overrides)
- Canonical call patterns:
  - Direct variable call: worker({message = "..."})
  - Lookup call: Agent("worker")({message = "..."}) (supported by AgentLookup)
- Return shape: document what result fields are stable (e.g. result.output, result.response) and how to access them; verify against runtime.
- Per-turn overrides:
  - tools overrides (primary)
  - optional generation params if supported
- Observable behavior over text:
  - tool calls + procedure state + bounded loops + done tool
- Mocking:
  - Mocks { worker = { tool_calls = [...], message = "..." } }
  - Run: tactus test file.tac --mock

Chapter 08-tool-integration.qmd (tool plumbing)
- Tool definition patterns:
  - Tool { description, input schema, function(args) ... }
- Toolset patterns:
  - Toolset { type = "lua", tools = {...} }
  - Toolset { use = "mcp.<server>", tools = {...} } (and mock-mode placeholder behavior if relevant)
- Composition:
  - Agent { tools = {toolset1, tool2, done} }
  - Per-turn restriction via tools = {...}
- Testing:
  - mock tools + deterministic tool results
  - mock agents where needed

Doc tone
- Programming-Tactus is deep reference: be precise about what is supported today.
- Avoid speculative APIs (e.g. Agent("name").turn()) unless verified.
